# Roost Animation — Researcher Journeys & Scientific Examples

**Companion to:** `roost_animation_discovery.md` (first-pass discovery; corrections from it are listed in §7 and were applied to that file).
**Scope of this document:** three evidence-backed researcher journeys, the *actual* app experience behind each, animation-ready data exports (in `docs/animation/`), a comparison, and a recommended 60–75 s sequence.
**Nothing here was implemented as animation; no application code was modified.** Exports are small derived data files generated by one-off scripts from live artifacts on 2026-11-10.

Legend used throughout: **[VERIFIED]** = read directly from a repository artifact this session; **[UI]** = confirmed rendered by the live application (source-audited); **[ANIM-ONLY]** = visual that does not exist in the app and would be an animation-only representation; **[HYPOTHESIS]** = unvalidated scientific interpretation.

---

## 0. Corrections & verifications performed first (gating example choices)

1. **Palaeognath ANP32A count corrected: 12, not 13.** The mesite (*Mesitornis unicolor*, Mesitornithiformes) is a **neognath** despite its ratite-like biology. Recount with standard palaeognath orders (Struthioniformes, Rheiformes, Casuariiformes, Apterygiformes, Tinamiformes): **12/12 palaeognaths with complete sequences lack the 33-aa insert; 316/334 (94.6%) complete neognath sequences carry it; 18 neognaths lack it** (387 complete avian sequences total; 60 more excluded as fragments). `web/public/data/anp32/comparison.json`. Export: `docs/animation/anp32a_insert_palaeognaths.csv`. Discovery report updated.
2. **DDX58 absence confidence quantified.** 245 not-found rows across 230 species; **47 rows / 39 species are HIGH confidence** (searchability ≥ 0.917), and **every one is a Phasianidae or Odontophoridae gamebird**. 177 rows are low confidence (incl. tinamous, the false lead from the first report). Boundary check within Galliformes [VERIFIED]: **cracid (*Penelope pileata*) and megapode (*Alectura lathami*) retain DDX58 (blast-found); guineafowl (*Numida meleagris*) shows a fragment; all 20 Anseriformes in the OrthoFinder set are FULL** (16 annotation + 4 blast). The loss is a *derived* event bounded to the higher gamebirds — this replaces the looser "galliform loss" framing. Exports: `ddx58_calls_galloanserae.csv`, `journey3_ddx58.json`.
3. **Presence dataset units resolved.** `gene_presence_v2.parquet` = 2,951,184 rows where **one row = (panel_version, taxon_id, assembly, gene_symbol)** — a gene×**assembly** call, not gene×species. 2,388 assemblies, 2,042 distinct taxon ids (2,093 species-name strings incl. subspecies labels like *Gallus gallus murghi*), 1,435 gene symbols (incl. controls), **three mixed panel versions** (v3.20261006 = 2.45 M rows; v3.20260907 = 503 k; v3.20260831 = 1.2 k legacy rows retained). Collapsed units: 2,758,464 distinct (species, gene) pairs; 2,689,192 (taxon, gene) pairs. `stats.json`'s 2,741,391 matches none of these exactly (older export filter) — cite `by_the_numbers.json` (21/21 checks green) or the parquet directly.
4. **Publication references verified 2026-11-10 (corrected where wrong):** Barber 2010 is actually **Barber, Aldridge, Webster & Magor, PNAS 107(13):5913–5918, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1001755107** — the corpus record carried a wrong title/journal/DOI (10.4049/jimmunol.0902471, 404s) and an unsupported "pseudogene" summary; corrected against PubMed PMID 20308570. Long 2019 *eLife* DOI corrected to 10.7554/eLife.45066 (the .001 suffix was a sub-article part DOI). ANP32A-editing chickens 2023 *Nat Commun* DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-41476-3 verified (Idoko-Akoh et al.). duck genome 2013 *Nat Genet* DOI 10.1038/ng.2657; goose OASL 2016 DOI 10.1089/jir.2015.0167. The corpus quote source `comparative_analysis_host_responses_2024` is Smith et al. **2015** BMC Genomics (record year corrected 2024→2015).
5. **Modeled vs measured susceptibility kept separate.** Two artifacts disagree for mallard [VERIFIED]: `host_competence.json` legacy composite says "highly_tolerant"; `species_susceptibility.json` **v2 (authoritative, two-axis)** says permissiveness 85.8 → "highly_susceptible" *class* — i.e. highly **permissive** (easily infected — exactly what a reservoir is), severity basis p75 from 1 study. The animation must say "permissive" and label the score MODELED, never "resistant/tolerant as measured fact". Both artifacts stamp `provenance: MEASURED (surveillance)` for detections and `MODELED (composite)` for scores.
6. **Spelling-variant trap found (three variants for one bird).** Kākāpō appears as `Strigops habroptila` (BirdTree newick + species_index) and `Strigops habroptilus` (susceptibility v2). My first report wrongly said kākāpō was absent from the tree — it is present (`Strigops_habroptila`). Any pipeline joining these artifacts needs a synonym step; the animation data files use the index spelling and note the variant.
7. **`species_index.json` `det` field is unreliable** (e.g. chicken "det: 182,165,286") — do not use; use `detections.parquet` / `host_competence` counts. Flagged as a data bug for the team.

## 1. Journey A — Species-first: *"What do we know about this species?"*

### Chosen species: mallard (*Anas platyrhynchos*) → contrast coda: kākāpō (*Strigops habroptila*)

Rejected alternatives: hoiho (*Megadyptes antipodes*) has **no genome and zero presence rows** [VERIFIED] — would show only coverage gaps; chicken is excellent but doubles as Journey C's payoff, so it appears here only as the pivot species.

**What the researcher actually finds [VERIFIED 2026-11-10 after the readiness pass — from `docs/animation/journey1_species.json`]:**

| | Mallard | Chicken (pivot) | Kākāpō (coda) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Taxon id | 8839 | 9031 | 2489341 |
| Surveillance detections | 1,838 records (1,836 dated) from 2006-02-23, 12 countries | 314 from 2021-11-05 | **0** |
| Genome | GCF_047663525.1 — **Complete Genome**, N50 80.2 Mb, annotated | GCF_016699485.2 — Chromosome, N50 90.9 Mb | GCA_004027225.2 — Chromosome |
| Panel calls (best per gene, 1,435 genes) | 1,352 FULL / 25 frag / 58 not-found | 1,416 / 4 / 15 | 1,278 / 55 / 102 |
| DDX58 (RIG-I) | **FULL (annotated)** | **NOT_FOUND — high confidence (s=1.00)** | **FULL (annotated)** |
| IFITM3 | FRAGMENT | FULL | NOT_FOUND — **low** confidence (s=0.667) |
| MX1 | FULL | FULL | NOT_FOUND — low confidence |
| Susceptibility v2 | permissiveness 85.8 → "highly_susceptible" class (= highly permissive reservoir), confidence 1.0 | 91.0, severe (22 severity studies) | **`unevaluated`**, confidence 0.0, literature-only |
| Literature | 18 papers (host_competence) | 87 papers | 0 surveillance; vaccination-program record (2 items, unclear outcomes) |
| Conservation | — | — | critically endangered, ~350 individuals (2025, DOC), vaccination target |

*(Canonical count definitions — see `docs/animation/scientific_readiness_report.md`: raw records = detections.parquet rows; the species grid badge now shows record counts after the flock-size bug fix; host_competence reports dated records.)*

**The scientifically honest story:** for mallard, Roost answers the question richly (measured surveillance history, complete genome, full innate panel, permissiveness model with provenance). For kākāpō, Roost's answer is *"we don't know — and here is exactly what evidence is missing"*: zero detections, `unevaluated` susceptibility, RIG-I present, but IFITM1/3 and MX1 non-detections at LOW confidence on a chromosome-level assembly [VERIFIED]. That is the resource's honesty: absence-of-evidence is rendered as absence-of-evidence, not as absence.

**Actual navigation (works today) [UI]:** `#/species` search "mallard" → card (PhyloPic silhouette, detection badge, assembly chip, risk chip) → `#/species/8839` modal, 5 tabs: **overview** (IUCN, links), **detections** (dates/sources), **genome**, **genes** (chips "{n} present / {n} fragment / {n} absent", key-gene grid with ✓/~/✗ linking to `#/genes/{sym}`; "View all N genes →" to `#/species-full/Anas%20platyrhynchos?tab=genes` with per-gene **EvidenceDrawer**: DIAMOND HSP viewer + thresholds + FASTA), **research** (paper conclusions as verbatim blockquotes with `#/papers/{id}` links). Kākāpō reachable identically (`#/species/2489341`, genome + genes tabs full).

**Not exposed in UI (animation must not imply it is) [VERIFIED gap]:** `absence_confidence`/`searchability` values are not rendered anywhere (only Methods mermaid + dashed "putative" chip borders distinguish evidence levels); per-species susceptibility component breakdown lives on `#/susceptibility/{name}`, not on the species modal; the count discrepancy 1,838/1,842 between artifacts is invisible to users.

**Suggested visual states:** species search typing "mallard" → card grid → modal genes tab with P/F/A chips; then the same shot sequence for "kākāpō" landing on `unevaluated` + zero detections. [ANIM-ONLY]: a "confidence dial" (searchability gauge) next to kākāpō's IFITM3 ✗ — the *value* exists in the parquet; the dial visualization does not.

## 2. Journey B — Literature-first: *"From 1,528 papers to a testable question"*

### Chosen bridge: IFITM3 — strong in-vivo literature in chickens vs. unresolved genomic distribution in birds

DDX58 is deliberately reserved for Journey C. IFITM3 gives a *different* and arguably more "reusable-resource" story: the literature is strong, and the genomics honestly says "we can't yet tell".

**The literature side [VERIFIED — quotes verbatim from `data/papers/gene_claims.jsonl`]:**
- *"The chIFITM3-overexpressing chicks showed significant protection and disease tolerance against highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) H5N1 (Clade 2.2.1.2)."* — central-tier claim, paper `smith_gannet2024_7` (in-vivo chick study).
- *"…siIFITM3 resulting in the most pronounced decrease (threefold)"* — `chicken_ifitm_ndv2025` (chIFITM3 required for IFN-λ3 antiviral activity).
- Evidence profile: **57 papers** linked to IFITM3, 45 of them reached **via alias resolution** (M1-, IFITM1/2 family names folded in), 40 reviewed-evidence items, 14 reviewed connections (`gene_evidence_counts.json`).
- Corpus backdrop: 1,528 papers, 1,860 verified LLM analyses, every claim stored with a verbatim quote + paper id; 89% of the 3,896 spread items are quote-grounded; model = local `muse-glimmer-30b` (extract → verify double-pass).

**The genomic side [VERIFIED]:** IFITM3 has **zero high-confidence absences anywhere in the 2,055-species panel** (contrasted with DDX58's 39). Its not-found calls sit at searchability 0.5–0.67 in zebra finch, collared flycatcher, tinamou, ostrich — *and kākāpō* (0.667, low) — while the mallard, the best-studied waterfowl, only shows a **fragment**. The research question practically writes itself: *is IFITM3 genuinely patchy across birds, or is its detection limited by assembly/annotation quality?* Roost surfaces exactly where the evidence is thin — and which genome assemblies would resolve it.

**Actual navigation (works today) [UI]:** `#/papers` → search/topic/year filters (topic chips incl. "Host Genomics", "Innate Immunity") → paper focus view with summary + DEG genes linking to `#/genes/{symbol}` → Genes grid (`IFITM3` card: 57-paper chip, connections badge) → `#/genes/IFITM3` gene page: "Literature evidence" section (`gene_evidence/IFITM3.json`: papers + mechanisms with paper links), wiki conclusions **as blockquotes with citations**, presence chips → EvidenceDrawer (DIAMOND HSPs, identity coloring, thresholds) → "View in phylogeny" → `#/phylogeny?gene=IFITM3` tree colored FULL/FRAGMENT/NOT_FOUND.

**Not exposed [VERIFIED gaps]:** there is no dedicated quote-browser — verbatim quotes appear as conclusion blockquotes and hover tooltips only; the *verification* step (extract→verify corrections) is backend-only (`data/papers/verified/*.json`); IFITM alias-resolved counts are not surfaced per gene page.

**Suggested visual states:** papers grid scrolling with topic filter → zoom into one paper card → the quote pulls forward (real quote, real citation) → gene page literature block → presence chips → phylogeny overlay with reds that carry a "low confidence" tag. [ANIM-ONLY]: the "LLM verify" moment (a checkmark drawing over the quote against source text) — the verification *result* is real data (`all_verified: true` in verified JSON); the animated verification *scene* is a representation, not a screen.

## 3. Journey C — Gene-first: DDX58 / RIG-I

**The full arc, all real [VERIFIED, exports `journey3_ddx58.json` + `ddx58_calls_galloanserae.csv` + `subtree_rigI_galloanserae.newick`]:**

1. **Literature:** 89 papers, 88 "studied" (not passing mentions), 16 reviewed connections, 50 reviewed evidence items; LLM dossier in `gene_profiles/DDX58.json` ("…galliform species lack a functional ortholog and show more severe HPAIV disease"). Key reference Barber et al. 2010 PNAS (DOI 10.1073/pnas.1001755107, corrected), plus the corpus quote: *"Chickens (but not ducks) lack the intracellular receptor for viral ssRNA, RIG-I…"* (Smith et al. 2015, BMC Genomics).
2. **Orthology:** OG0011985, high-confidence mapping (og_frac 1.0), orthologs recovered in 334 of 463 OrthoFinder species — RIG-I is broadly conserved in birds.
3. **Presence:** 2,093 species searched (best per species: ~1,792 full incl. annotated + found, 351 fragment rows, 245 not-found rows); **39 species high-confidence absence — every one a Phasianidae/Odontophoridae gamebird** (chicken s=1.00; turkey 0.917; both quail; peafowl; grouse; pheasants…).
4. **Phylogeny:** on the real 24-species Galloanserae subtree (BirdTree Ericson, real branch lengths), the loss maps as a **derived event**: cracid + megapode (basal galliforms) FULL, guineafowl fragment, all 12 sampled phasianid/odontophorid species NOT_FOUND, all anseriforms FULL. This *independently reproduces and bounds* the literature claim — and the guineafowl fragment hints at a graded loss at the family boundary [HYPOTHESIS — flag as interpretation, one species].

**Actual navigation (works today) [UI]:** `#/genes/DDX58` (literature sections, key-finding card, wiki synthesis, presence chips + EvidenceDrawer, orthogroup button `#/orthogroups/OG0011985`) → "View in phylogeny" `#/phylogeny?gene=DDX58` (tree colored FULL/FRAGMENT/NOT_FOUND, filtered to called species, counts shown; species click → modal) → `#/clade` gene×order matrix with cell drill-down (Galliformes row shows the loss as absence %).

**Not exposed [VERIFIED gaps]:** absence-confidence is not rendered on the tree/clade views (a NOT_FOUND at s=0.5 looks identical to one at s=1.0); the gene overlay on the phylogeny colors only *called* species without confidence shading; no per-family collapse.

**Suggested visual states:** gene page header with "89 papers" → literature blockquote → phylogeny `?gene=DDX58` opening with the gamebird clade going red branch-by-branch while waterfowl stay green; the cracid/megapode tips stay green *inside* the red clade — the derived-loss reveal. [ANIM-ONLY]: animating the loss event along internal branches (the data supports presence/absence at tips only; ancestral-state inference is NOT computed by Roost — any "loss event marker" on an internal branch must be drawn as illustration, clearly derived from the tip pattern).

## 4. Journey comparison

| Criterion | A. Species-first (mallard→kākāpō) | B. Literature-first (IFITM3) | C. Gene-first (DDX58) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scientific accuracy | ★★★★★ (all measured; kākāpō honestly `unevaluated`) | ★★★★ (quotes verbatim; question framed as open) | ★★★★★ (established + independently bounded loss) |
| User relevance | ★★★★★ (the exact question every visitor has) | ★★★★ (researchers planning comparative studies) | ★★★★ (immunologists, poultry) |
| Visual clarity | ★★★ (page-tour shape; least cinematic) | ★★★★ (quotes→tree transition is strong) | ★★★★★ (tree lights up = instant payoff) |
| Data completeness | ★★★★★ | ★★★★ (no quote-browser UI) | ★★★★★ |
| Shows Roost's reusable-resource value | ★★★★ | ★★★★★ (corpus + verification is the moat) | ★★★★ |
| Risk | mallard artifact drift (1,838/1,842; tolerant/permissive wording) | zero high-confidence absences must be *explained*, not hidden | internal-branch loss marker would be inference — keep at tips |

## 5. Recommended 60–75 s sequence (three questions, one resource)

Unifying device: **the same tree stays on screen between acts**, re-colored three ways — presence/surveillance/confidence — so the piece reads as one resource answering three questions, not three demos. LLM appears twice, briefly, as the bridge that makes evidence machine-usable.

| Time | Beat | Content | Reality basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–8 s | **The question** | Detections map pulses (44,931 records, 106 countries; 2022 wave). "Which birds are at risk — and how would we know?" | [VERIFIED] `detections.parquet`; `#/map` exists [UI] |
| 8–22 s | **Journey A** | Species search: "mallard" → page: 1,838 detections since 2006, complete genome, 1,352/1,435 panel genes, permissive reservoir (MODELED label visible). Search: "kākāpō" → **zero detections, `unevaluated`**, ~350 birds, RIG-I present. "For some species, the honest answer is: unknown." | [UI] routes real; [ANIM-ONLY] confidence dial |
| 22–24 s | **Bridge** | "What does the literature say?" — papers grid → one PDF → **extract → verify** moment with the real IFITM3 chick-protection quote | quote [VERIFIED]; verify-scene [ANIM-ONLY] |
| 24–36 s | **Journey B** | Corpus stats strip (1,528 papers · 4,348 genes · 8,631 links · quotes verbatim) → `#/genes/IFITM3` → phylogeny overlay: greens, ambers, reds **tagged low-confidence**. "Sometimes the answer is: the evidence isn't there yet." | [UI] real; confidence tags [ANIM-ONLY] |
| 36–52 s | **Journey C — payoff** | "Ask a sharper question." `#/genes/DDX58` (89 papers) → tree: RIG-I present across the tree… then the gamebird clade goes dark — 39 high-confidence absences — while cracid, megapode, and every duck stay green. Duck vs chicken split-screen. | [VERIFIED]; branch-event marker [ANIM-ONLY, tip-derived] |
| 52–62 s | **The resource** | Fast montage, real screens: model graph, orthogroups, ANP32 page, clade matrix, downloads. Numbers strip: 2,951,184 presence calls (gene×assembly) · 2,055 species · 40,494 orthogroups · 9,993-species tree. | [UI] all routes exist |
| 62–75 s | **Coda** | Kākāpō silhouette (PhyloPic, credited) on the tree. "Literature, genomics, phylogeny — one reusable resource. roost… (site URL)" | silhouette [VERIFIED, license check needed] |

LLM screen-time ≈ 6–8 s of 75 — visible, but the star is the connected evidence.

## 7. Separation of fact / design / hypothesis (summary)

- **[VERIFIED facts]** all numbers above with artifact citations; every quote verbatim from `gene_claims.jsonl`; UI behaviors from component source audit.
- **[Proposed animation design]** the 75-second sequence, act structure, tree-recolor device, montage; confidence dials; verify-scene; split-screen duck/chicken.
- **[Unvalidated hypotheses — must be labeled or omitted]** (1) ANP32A palaeognath absence pattern — Roost measurement, MSA-derived, needs sequence spot-check before featuring; (2) guineafowl fragment as "graded loss at family boundary" — one species; (3) DDX58 Z-linkage sex-bias — explicitly "Untested — G6" in `avian_h5n1_model.json`; (4) any internal-branch loss-event animation — tip data only, no ancestral reconstruction computed.

---

## 8. Unresolved scientific / technical issues for the team

1. **Mallard susceptibility wording across artifacts** (`host_competence` "highly_tolerant" vs v2 "highly_susceptible[=permissive]") — needs a UI/terminology reconciliation before any public-facing use; both files ship today.
2. **Detection counts drift** between `detections.parquet` (1,838 mallard / 314 chicken) and `host_competence.json` (1,842 / 310) — snapshot timing; decide one canonical source for animation captions.
3. **`species_index.det` field corrupt** (chicken 182,165,286) — bug to file; animation must not read it.
4. **Spelling variants** (`Strigops habroptila`/`habroptilus`) — synonym map needed for any cross-artifact join in production tooling.
5. **`absence_confidence`/`searchability` unexposed in UI** — if the animation leans on confidence (it should), consider whether the UI should grow a small confidence affordance so the animation doesn't show more than the product delivers; otherwise caption as "from the pipeline dataset".
6. ~~Barber 2010 pseudogene vs deletion wording~~ **RESOLVED 2026-11-10**: the "pseudogene" wording was an unsupported LLM confabulation under wrong metadata; the corrected record (verified against the PNAS abstract) says RIG-I "**may be absent**" in chickens. Animation wording: "chickens have lost functional RIG-I" is safe; "pseudogene" and "deletion" are not established by these data.
7. **PhyloPic licensing**: attribution strings exist per image; per-image license verification still outstanding (many records have `license: null`).
8. **No dedicated quotes browser** — Journey B's strongest asset (verbatim evidence) is backend-only; a future UI feature candidate.
